highlightAliases.new: Acetaminophen: the ACR/AF OA guideline uses a conservative 3 g/day maximum for regular treatment, with monitoring and lower limits when indicated. The FDA general adult ceiling across all products is 4 g in 24 hours. Follow the lower product- or patient-specific limit, especially with liver disease, low body weight or substantial alcohol exposure (p787; FDA, ACR/AF OA guideline).

highlightAliases.old: Intra-articular glucocorticoid: pain relief up to 2 months; no more than 3 injections per 6-month period (p789).
highlightAliases.new: Intra-articular glucocorticoids may relieve pain for up to 2 months. Hazzard discourages more than three injections in six months (p789). Repeat injections are individualized. EULAR describes a customary limit of 3–4 per joint per year, while acknowledging limited evidence for a precise safe frequency (EULAR intra-articular therapy recommendations, 2021).

highlightAliases.old: No more than 3 injections within a 6-month period; pain relief typically lasts up to 2 months (p789).
highlightAliases.new: Hazzard advises against more than three injections in six months and describes pain relief lasting up to two months (p789). EULAR cites a customary limit of 3–4 injections in the same joint per year, with limited evidence for a universal safe count.

highlightAliases.old: ~240 million worldwide have symptomatic OA; ≥32 million in the US. OA is the 3rd leading cause of years lived with disability in the US and the most common cause of mobility limitation in older adults (p779).
highlightAliases.new: The chapter estimates ~240 million people worldwide with symptomatic OA and ≥32 million in the US. In the data it cites, OA ranked third for years lived with disability in the US and was the most common cause of mobility limitation in older adults (p779).

highlightAliases.old: Genetics: 90 genome-wide significant OA risk loci identified; COL2A1 (type II collagen) is among the implicated genes (p780).
highlightAliases.new: Genetics: 90 genome-wide significant OA risk loci reported in the studies available to the chapter; COL2A1 (type II collagen) is among the implicated genes (p780).

highlightAliases.old: Viscosupplementation (IA hyaluronic acid): not recommended by ACR/AF/OARSI (p789). Platelet-rich plasma/mesenchymal stem cell therapy: still experimental and not FDA-approved — only within an FDA-approved trial (p789); ACR/AF strongly against for knee/hip (Figure 52-5, p786).
highlightAliases.new: Viscosupplementation (intra-articular hyaluronic acid) has little clear benefit in low-bias trials. ACR/AF recommends against it for knee OA, while OARSI allows selected knee use depending on comorbidities (p789 and the guideline comparison above). Hazzard advises restricting PRP and mesenchymal stem-cell treatments to trials (p789). ACR/AF recommends against both for knee and hip OA. For symptomatic knee OA specifically, AAOS gives limited support to PRP for pain and function because trial results vary. These treatments have not been shown to restore lost cartilage. AAOS knee OA guideline, Platelet-rich Plasma.

highlightAliases.old: At least 32 million people (out of ~240 million worldwide with symptomatic OA); OA is the 3rd leading cause of years lived with disability in the US (p779).
highlightAliases.new: The chapter reports at least 32 million people in the US and about 240 million worldwide. OA ranked third for years lived with disability in the US estimates it cites (p779).

highlightAliases.old: Glucosamine and chondroitin sulfate (no more effective than placebo in the lowest-bias data), TNF inhibitors and IL-1 receptor antagonists (not efficacious for erosive OA), and bisphosphonates (no efficacy for pain or function) (p788; Figure 52-5, p786).
highlightAliases.new: Glucosamine for hand, hip or knee OA, and chondroitin sulfate for hip or knee OA. Hand OA is an exception: ACR/AF conditionally recommends chondroitin sulfate for this site. Other drugs recommended against include TNF inhibitors and IL-1 receptor antagonists (not efficacious for erosive OA), and bisphosphonates (no efficacy for pain or function) (p788; Figure 52-5, p786).
